messages:
maya: anyone seeing TLS handshake failures on Windows when using the python sdk on 3.8/3.9? started after we bumped httpx and the async client. stack trace is just SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED :/
sam: yep, saw this locally on Win10 + py3.8 in a conda env. repro minimal:
```python
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key=\"x\")
    await c.generate(\"hi\")

asyncio.run(main())
```
error occurs during first request (connect).

jess: I hit a similar one but it was caused by our env having an empty REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE variable set by an internal script. if you unset that or point it to certifi.where() it worked. on Windows the system cert store + some venv combos are funky. try:
```py
import certifi, ssl
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
# pass ctx into httpx if you create a client manually
```

sam: tried forcing certifi, still got one case where httpx/ssl used SCHANNEL and still failed — only reproducible on py3.9. looked like load_verify_locations(None) behaviour differs by minor py version. attaching the short log:
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:997)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
httpx.ConnectError: ... caused by SSLError
```

ryan: maybe the sdk should detect common Windows combos and prefer a bundled cafile or at least provide a clear env var hint. also we don't have any docs for Windows troubleshooting in the quickstart. can we add a short note + an env-hook in the client that prints a helpful hint when verify fails? (non-fatal is ok) :thinking_face:

maya: yes please. this was a painful onboarding moment for a new customer. they were on py3.10 on linux and fine, only hit on windows with 3.8/3.9 in CI.

jess: small typing/async nit: when folks try to import AsyncClient in py3.8 you get weird Mypy complaints unless they install types-httpx + from __future__ import annotations. could we add a stub package or relax some annotations to keep 3.8 users happier?

sam: filed a quick internal bug: RDW-4621 with reproduction steps + logs. proposal: 1) detect certifi and use certifi.where() by default on Windows 2) add env REDWOOD_USE_BUNDLED_CA (true/false) 3) surface a one-line hint on SSL errors pointing to the doc page. also add a short example in the sdk README for how to create an ssl.SSLContext for httpx/asyncio.

ryan: +1. can we also add a small unit test matrix in CI that runs a smoke request on Windows runner for py3.8/3.9/3.10? catch regressions early.

infra-bot: CI: windows-smoke (py38) failed on job 5123 at 2026-03-15T14:02:10Z — failing test: tests/integration/test_networking.py::test_basic_generate

maya: ok i'll take the docs + hint patch. sam do you want the SDK change (auto detect/use bundled) or should that go to infra/serving team for review?

sam: i'll open a PR in the sdk repo with the detection + env toggle. keep it behind a feature-flag for now and add an entry in CHANGELOG. will include unit + an integration smoke (skipped unless RUN_WINDOWS_SMOKE=true).

jess: for typing: we could ship types in the package (py.typed) and add our minimal stubs for AsyncClient generics to smooth Mypy on older pythons. low-effort and big UX win.

maya: yep. prioritizing: 1) quick docs + troubleshooting snippet 2) env toggle + opt-in detection PR 3) typing stubs. thanks all :party_parrot:

sam: follow-ups: i'll paste the PR link here when ready and link the customer repro. in the meantime workaround for anyone stuck: export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=$(python -c 'import certifi; print(certifi.where())') or set REDWOOD_USE_BUNDLED_CA=true in env for the dev machine.

ryan: would be great if the error message included that exact command. tiny DX improvement = fewer support tickets.

maya: filed a short doc page at docs/devex/windows-ssl.md and added the command. leaving thread open for PR links.

infra-bot: ticket RDW-4621 updated: assigned sam -> in progress

sam: posting PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/278 : includes detection, env toggle, and tests. please review.
